questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x?$ Assume $n$ is an integer.

I. The function has vertical asymptotes at $x=\pi +\frac{n\pi }{2}.$

II. The domain of the function is $[-\pi ,\pi ].$

III. The period of the function is $\pi .$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's plot the graph of $y=cot⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934292/assets/7785ad73f6e5212772c3053780ffd055f37cfb39927b6ddc3e40cd3a55b8ba4e.png)

Now, let's go through each statement.

- Statement I is false. The vertical asymptotes of the function are integer multiples of $\pi $, i.e., $x=n\pi .$

- Statement II is false. The domain of the function is all real numbers except the values where the asymptotes occur, i.e., $x=n\pi .$

- Statement III is true. The period of $y=cot⁡x$ is $\pi .$

Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x?$ Assume $n$ is an integer.

I. The function has no minimum value. $$

II. $x=-4\pi $ is in the domain of the function. $$

III. $x=-\frac{3\pi }{2}$ is a zero of the function.

Now, let's go through each statement.

- Statement I is true. The function has no minimum or maximum value. $$

- Statement II is false. The function is defined for all real numbers except the values $n\pi $ for any integer $n$, thus it is not defined for $x=-4\pi .$

- Statement III is true. The zeros of $y=cot⁡x$ occur at $\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,$ for any integer $n.$ Therefore, $x=-\frac{3\pi }{2}$ is a zero of the function.

questions.knowledge_point: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cotangent Function
questions.problem: If $cot⁡x=-4$ for some $x,$ then find the value of $3cot⁡(x+17\pi )+6.$
questions.worked_solution:
The period of $y=cot⁡x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for any integer $n,$ we have

$$
cot⁡x=cot⁡(x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=17$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡x & =cot⁡(x+17\cdot \pi ) \\  & =cot⁡(x+17\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $cot⁡x=-4,$ then $cot⁡(x+17\pi )=-4.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}3cot⁡(x+7\pi )+6 & =3(-4)+6 \\  & =-12+6 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: If $cot⁡x=\sqrt{2}$ for some $x,$ then find the value of $cot⁡(x-9\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
The period of $y=cot⁡x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for any integer $n,$ we have

$$
cot⁡x=cot⁡(x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-9$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡x & =cot⁡(x+(-9)\cdot \pi ) \\  & =cot⁡(x-9\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $cot⁡x=\sqrt{2},$ then $cot⁡(x-9\pi )=\sqrt{2}.$

questions.problem: If $cot⁡x=\sqrt{3}$ for some $x$, then find the value of $\sqrt{3}cot⁡(x-\pi )-4.$
questions.worked_solution:
The period of $y=cot⁡x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
cot⁡x=cot⁡(x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-1$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡x=cot⁡(x+(-1)\cdot \pi )=cot⁡(x-\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $cot⁡x=\sqrt{3},$ then $cot⁡(x-\pi )=\sqrt{3}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}cot⁡(x-\pi )-4 & =\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3})-4 \\  & ={(\sqrt{3})}^{2}-4 \\  & =3-4 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: If $cot⁡x=\sqrt{5}$ for some $x$, then find the value of $2\sqrt{5}cot⁡(x-3\pi )-8.$
questions.worked_solution:
The period of $y=cot⁡x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
cot⁡x=cot⁡(x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-3$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡x=cot⁡(x+(-3)\cdot \pi )=cot⁡(x-3\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $cot⁡x=\sqrt{5},$ then $cot⁡(x-3\pi )=\sqrt{5}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{5}cot⁡(x-3\pi )-8 & =2\sqrt{5}(\sqrt{5})-8 \\  & =2{(\sqrt{5})}^{2}-8 \\  & =10-8 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Utilizing the Oddness Property of the Cotangent Function
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=cot⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934292/assets/6eb672fe024f024f20c7c3c80947d1b47bade8f998e705d6f411ae3f298ecde2.png)

From the graph, we note the following:

- The period of $cot⁡x$ is $\pi .$

- Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $cot⁡x$ is an *odd* function, and we have

$$
cot⁡(-x)=-cot⁡x.
$$

Let's now evaluate our expression:

- Firstly, using the periodicity of $cot⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡(-a+5\pi ) & =cot⁡(-a+\pi \cdot 5) \\  & =cot⁡(-a).\end{aligned}
$$

- Secondly, using the oddness of $cot⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡(-a) & =-cot⁡a \\  & =-(-7) \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $cot⁡(-a+5\pi )=7.$

- The function has zeros at $x = \pi n,$ where $n$ is an integer.

- The function has asymptotes at $x = \pm\dfrac \pi 2, \pm \dfrac {3 \pi} 2,\dots$

- The range of $y = \cot x$ is $(-\infty,-1] \cup [1,\infty).$

canonical_examples.problem: If $\cot x = 1$ for some $x,$ then find the value of $\cot(x+5\pi).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The period of $y = \cot x$ is $\pi.$ Therefore, for any integer $n,$ we have

$$
\cot{x} = \cot{(x+n\pi)} .
$$

Substituting $n=5$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡x & =cot⁡(x+5\cdot \pi ) \\  & =cot⁡(x+5\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\cot{x} = 1,$ then $\cot{(x+5\pi)} = 1.$

canonical_examples.problem: If $\cot x = 2,$ then what is the value of $\cot (-x+7\pi)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\cot{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934292/assets/6eb672fe024f024f20c7c3c80947d1b47bade8f998e705d6f411ae3f298ecde2.png)

From the graph, we note the following:

- The period of $\cot{x}$ is $\pi.$

- Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\cot{x}$ is an *odd* function, and we have

$$
\cot(-x) = -\cot{x}.
$$

Let's now evaluate our expression:

- Firstly, using the periodicity of $\cot{x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡(-x+7\pi ) & =cot⁡(-x+\pi \cdot 7) \\  & =cot⁡(-x).\end{aligned}
$$

- Secondly, using the oddness of $\cot{x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}cot⁡(-x) & =-cot⁡x \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\cot (-x+7\pi)=-2.$
